edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct TWO COUNTING ERRORS in this otherwise attractive Đông Hồ Vietnamese Lê palace sprite. Preserve every other building, color, warm-black contour, camera, compact footprint and arrangement exactly.
1. FOREGROUND MASONRY GATE: it currently has SEVEN arched portals, which is historically wrong for the Đoan Môn-inspired gate. Rebuild only this strip with EXACTLY FIVE arched portals: two left of centre, one broad centre, two right of centre. Five openings total, count 1 2 3 4 5. Close the extra two portals with matching solid brick-and-stone wall. Give only those five portals their small front steps. No additional small hidden arches.
2. MAIN HALL STAIRCASE: it currently has six dragon railings and five narrow stairs. Replace that staircase with EXACTLY FOUR dragon balustrades delimiting EXACTLY THREE broad parallel stair approaches. Four long stone dragon railings, three lanes: railing / left stair / railing / centre stair / railing / right stair / railing. Not six railings.
Keep all the other roofs and side galleries. Background, courtyards and empty portal holes must be genuine transparent alpha, NOT a drawn checkerboard. No text or labels. This is a correction of architecture, not a new design.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target, an otherwise attractive Đông Hồ Nguyễn imperial precinct. Image 2 is an official Huế Tourism Department photograph of the real Ngọ Môn, used ONLY to correct the gate's configuration. Do not copy the photo's nighttime illumination or realism.
Correct the FRONT GATE in image 1 to match real Ngọ Môn: there must be EXACTLY THREE passages visible on the central front elevation. The two arches currently facing forward in the far-left and far-right protruding wings are WRONG. Close BOTH of these front-facing wing arches with solid matching masonry. The projecting front ends of both wings must be unbroken solid brick-and-stone walls under their green pavilion roofs. The other two passageways belong in the SIDE RETURNS of the U-shaped platform, running perpendicular to the three centre passages; if hidden by this camera angle, leave them hidden rather than showing extra front arches. Total historical entrances five; only three face the viewer. Use the attached photo to understand this geometry.
The central imperial door may have gold-yellow timber doors; the immediately flanking two have red timber doors, like the photo. Retain the graceful two-storey Ngũ Phụng profile, yellow central roof and green wing roofs, and the unchanged golden Thái Hòa hall behind it. Preserve all other buildings, footprint, frontal elevated orthographic camera, flat pigment and warm-black Đông Hồ outlines. No text, modern flags or scenery. Genuine transparent alpha outside the structure and in courtyard gaps, no baked checkerboard.
